summary: Self-hosted AI coding assistant, an open-source, on-premises alternative to GitHub Copilot that runs on consumer GPUs.

heroCommands.command:
docker run -it \
  --gpus all -p 8080:8080 -v $HOME/.tabby:/data \
  tabbyml/tabby \
  serve --model StarCoder-1B --device cuda --chat-model Qwen2-1.5B-Instruct

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Tabby is a self-hosted AI coding assistant. It gives code completion and chat in your editor from a server you run yourself, as an open-source, on-premises alternative to GitHub Copilot.
sixtySeconds.problem: Cloud coding assistants send your code to someone else. Tabby keeps it on your own hardware.
whoFor: Companies that can't send code to the cloud
Teams wanting a private Copilot alternative
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a self-contained server with no database or cloud service needed, an OpenAPI interface and support for consumer-grade GPUs.
requirements: Docker with GPU support (NVIDIA, for the example command)
An editor extension for your IDE

overview: The quickest start is one Docker command that serves a completion model (StarCoder-1B) and a chat model (Qwen2-1.5B-Instruct) on port 8080 using CUDA.
Then install the Tabby extension for your IDE or editor and point it at your server. Installation, extensions and configuration are covered in the docs.
Tabby is self-contained, with no DBMS or cloud service needed. Most of the code is open source; some portions use a separate license, so see the LICENSE file.
limitations: Needs a GPU for good speed
Small local models are less capable than big cloud ones
